question: According to the passage, where does a currency note's value come from?
options: The gold kept by the government
The shared belief that others will accept it

group.title: Reading comprehension
group.setup: The value of a currency note lies not in the paper but in the shared belief that others will accept it. This belief is fragile in an odd way: it survives ordinary shocks easily, yet it can collapse quickly once people expect others to lose faith. Central banks therefore guard their credibility as carefully as their reserves. A promise to keep prices stable is useful only if people believe it will be kept even when keeping it is painful. Paradoxically, the less a central bank needs to act to prove its resolve, the stronger that resolve appears.
